title: Detection histories of 58 Bombus impatiens nests on five surveys a year in coastal Massachusetts, 2018-2024
creator: Thuma, Jessie; Pugesek, Genevieve; Treanore, Erin; Finn, Sylvana; Crone, Elizabeth
citation: Thuma, J., Pugesek, G., Treanore, E., Finn, S., & Crone, E. (2025). Bumble bee nest density is lower in drought years [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.6t1g1jxbn
abstract: Detection (0/1) of each Bombus impatiens nest found on five nest surveys per season in meadow, forest and hayfield habitat in coastal Massachusetts, 2018-2024, with habitat: the mark-recapture input for nest abundance and apparent survival under drought.
samplingProtocol: Five systematic nest searches per season in a fixed survey area (meadow, forest, hayfield); each nest found is marked and re-detected or not on later surveys.
closureNote: nests within a season can die between surveys (the authors estimate apparent survival); each nest exists in one year
geographicCoverage: Coastal Massachusetts, USA (see the paper); no coordinates deposited

notShipped.rare_species: 9 nests of B. bimaculatus (2), B. perplexus (2), B. vagans (1), B. fervidus (1) and unidentified (1): too few per species for a table

notes: Unit = nest; rows only in the nest's year. One of two species tables from this deposit (the other is thuma_2025_ma_bgriseocollis_nest_cr).
